name: Kho ca dua
summary: Khô cá dứa is the dried sea catfish people carry out of Cần Giờ. Dân Việt, 28 Apr 2024, describes the one-sun fish: split, washed, salted at about 10 kg of fish to 1 kg of salt for about an hour, washed again, and dried for one sun. Sài Gòn Giải Phóng and Tuổi Trẻ both call it a specialty. Their counts do not match, and the 2016 prices do not match. A 2026 price is Check on arrival.
origin: Can Gio. Dân Việt, 28 Apr 2024. Sài Gòn Giải Phóng, 17 Feb 2014. Tuổi Trẻ, 14 Oct 2016.
howToEat: Dân Việt says fry it or grill it. The same story also names gỏi khô cá dứa, cơm cháy khô cá dứa, cơm vắt khô cá dứa, and a soup, without a method for those plates.

Sài Gòn Giải Phóng, 17 Feb 2014, prints one company and 25 processors, and 36 tons a year at the company that had registered a mark. Tuổi Trẻ, 14 Oct 2016, prints 60 producers and about 150 tons a year, vacuum packed, labeled, and kept 3–6 months. Both counts stay.

Tuổi Trẻ the same day prints three prices: city shops advertising 200,000–250,000 VND a kilogram, a maker’s line that 150,000–200,000 is not the real fish, and a district figure of 370,000–470,000. A 2026 price is Check on arrival.
where: A stall address was not printed. Tuổi Trẻ says buy from a producer the district supervises. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Kho ca dua — one-sun dried fish from Can Gio
seoDescription: One-sun khô cá dứa from Can Gio. Dân Việt prints the salt and the sun. Tuổi Trẻ, 14 Oct 2016, prints three prices that do not match. A 2026 price is Check on arrival.
texture: Dân Việt says one sun leaves the flesh yellow, firm, and without a fishy smell.
Tuổi Trẻ, quoting a maker in Cần Thạnh, says the real dried fish has only a little fat under the skin and fries or grills to a deep yellow. Dried tra or basa, the story says, weeps fat and goes soft.
